entities.name: Sakir-Har
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sakir-Har, whose name is primarily preserved on a doorjamb from Gebelein and on a scarab, reigned as one of the earliest Hyksos kings of the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt, likely in the early 16th century BCE. His brief but foundational rule marked a critical juncture in the Second Intermediate Period, as the Hyksos consolidated their control over Avaris and established a new foreign dynasty that profoundly challenged the traditional pharaonic order in Lower Egypt. He is significant as one of the first identifiable rulers of the Hyksos "Great House," signaling the shift from a period of Asiatic infiltration to overt political dominance in the Nile Delta.

While specific events of Sakir-Har's reign are scarce, his existence as attested by archaeological finds confirms the early establishment of the Hyksos Fifteenth Dynasty, headquartered at Avaris (modern Tell el-Dab'a). This period saw the Hyksos, a Semitic-speaking people, expand their influence from the eastern Delta, initially through trade and gradual settlement, into a formidable political power. Sakir-Har's rule would have involved the administration of a state apparatus distinct from the native Egyptian Twelfth and Thirteenth Dynasties, likely integrating foreign administrative practices with existing Egyptian structures in the northern territories he controlled.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sakir-Har's early reign solidified the Hyksos presence in Lower Egypt, laying the groundwork for the Fifteenth Dynasty's century-long rule and contributing to the profound political fragmentation of Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period.
